A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same FusionRoute study, including the main text and Appendices A–C. Text, equations, tables and embedded graphics support a reliable comparison. Figure 4 is clipped in v3, but its underlying graphic and caption remain recoverable.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, GPT-4o response-quality comparisons, training ablations and qualitative routing examples in Sections 5–6 and Appendix C.2.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results for the Llama-3 and Gemma-2 families, including the ablations and appendix routing examples.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 7, and Section 3.2.3 replace L_LM with L_expert for SFT samples during mixed training. These are distinct losses defined in Section 3.2.1, so this corrects the stated training objective and resolves v2's inconsistent routing-loss reference. The architecture and CDPO objective remain unchanged; no experimental rerun is established.

E1.justification: Both versions use PerfectBlend and OpenHermes for training and retain evaluations on GSM8K, MATH500, MBPP, HumanEval, IFEval and held-out PerfectBlend prompts. No task or data-domain coverage changes.

E2.justification: The expert models, Sequence Selection, Collab, Fine-tuned Model, DARE, Task Arithmetic and ablation comparators remain in their corresponding comparisons. The newly cited R2R work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C.1 retain the same splits, model checkpoints, training budgets, greedy decoding, benchmark sample counts, generation limits and 500-prompt GPT-4o evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Both retain the complementary-logit ablation in Table 2, the CDPO training ablation in Figure 4 and the routing case studies in Appendix C.2. Figure 4's relocation and clipping do not remove or revise the underlying analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the embedded charts in Figures 3–4 retain their scores and rankings. For example, FusionRoute's Table 1 average accuracies remain 0.566 for Llama-3 and 0.426 for Gemma-2. Appendix C.2's qualitative examples and findings also match.

T1.justification: Section 4's assumptions and bounds, Appendix A's proof and Appendix B's counterexample are retained. Appendix B replaces h with t in action and value-function subscripts, an equivalent indexing cleanup rather than revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about expert-only routing limitations, complementary generation, performance, robustness and efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of expert failures, complementary logits, model-scale differences and qualitative routing behavior remain unchanged, as do the qualifications concerning expert coverage.

D1.justification: Checkpoint and reward-model identifiers, hyperparameters, data-sampling instructions, the evaluation prompt and project/code-access information are unchanged. No additional implementation or resource disclosures appear.

R1.justification: Section 7.1 and the references add Fu et al. (2025), R2R. The previous CO-LLM-specific description of a strong math expert becomes a broader description of single-expert assistance covering both cited works, while FusionRoute's stated distinction remains.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the date/version text, loss references, Appendix B's index notation and the related-work paragraph. The section order and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reduced and several existing figures, tables and Algorithm 1 are repositioned, while their display designs remain intact. Figure 4 moves from v2 page 14 to v3 page 13, clipping its bottom labels and placing its caption outside the visible page.

improvement.justification: v3 improves methodological clarity by correcting the mixed-training loss reference and modestly broadens related-work coverage. However, its reflow clips Figure 4's labels and hides the caption, weakening presentation of the CDPO ablation. With the results and theory otherwise unchanged, these opposing benefits and harms do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
